title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #3

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When you say 'leaf' and 'leave' aloud, what is the last sound of 'leave'? (1 mark)
   A. /f/
   B. /t/
   C. /v/
   D. /d/

2. Which word begins with the blend tw? (1 mark)
   A. tennis
   B. tenth
   C. tender
   D. twenty

3. The word 'the' is said as 'thee' before (1 mark)
   A. a vowel sound
   B. a plural only
   C. a consonant sound
   D. a name

4. Which of these words has /r/ as its first sound? (1 mark)
   A. light
   B. load
   C. ribbon
   D. lake

5. Which word rhymes with 'road'? (1 mark)
   A. rod
   B. load
   C. raid
   D. lead

6. In a plan for a story, the middle usually tells (1 mark)
   A. only the title
   B. the last sentence
   C. what happens
   D. the name of the school

7. In the pattern 'enough + noun + to + verb', the word after 'to' is a (1 mark)
   A. verb
   B. adjective
   C. name
   D. noun

8. Complete: 'Mother bought enough flour ___ chapati.' (1 mark)
   A. to make
   B. making
   C. for make
   D. by make

9. In 'listen', the silent letter is (1 mark)
   A. t
   B. n
   C. s
   D. l

10. First aid is (1 mark)
   A. the first help given to a person who is hurt or ill
   B. a road sign
   C. a kind of food
   D. the last help

11. Pronouns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. The house is ours's.
   B. The house is ours'.
   C. The house is our's.
   D. The house is ours.

12. A friendly letter is written to (1 mark)
   A. nobody
   B. someone you know well
   C. a stranger only
   D. the government only

13. Which word begins the greeting in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Sincerely
   B. Faithfully
   C. Yours
   D. Dear

14. A reading log helps you to (1 mark)
   A. break books
   B. hide your books
   C. sell books
   D. remember what you have read

15. Which is a good rule for a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. Tear pages
   B. Talk all the time
   C. Listen politely and take turns
   D. Take books home and keep them

16. Adjectives: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. This is beautifullest than that.
   B. This is more beautifuler than that.
   C. This is beautifuller than that.
   D. This is more beautiful than that.

17. Which is the correct order for the parts of a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. Middle, end, beginning
   B. End, middle, beginning
   C. Beginning, middle, end
   D. End, beginning, middle

18. Intonation: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. full
   B. good
   C. put
   D. computer

19. In a written dialogue, the speaker's name is usually followed by (1 mark)
   A. a bracket
   B. a colon
   C. a full stop only
   D. nothing

20. What must every sentence begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A comma
   C. A capital letter
   D. A question mark

21. Which sentence is in the past tense? (1 mark)
   A. Baraka clicks Send.
   B. Baraka will click Send.
   C. Baraka clicked Send.
   D. Baraka is clicking Send.

22. Which sentence shows a habit in the present tense? (1 mark)
   A. I asked my mother yesterday.
   B. I had asked my mother.
   C. I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   D. I was asking my mother.

23. Which helping verb completes: 'I ____ writing a letter now.'? (1 mark)
   A. is
   B. was
   C. are
   D. am

24. Which sentence uses the past progressive correctly? (1 mark)
   A. I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   B. I was walk to school when it started to rain.
   C. I walking to school when it started to rain.
   D. I am walking to school when it started to rain.

25. What is the contraction of 'cannot'? (1 mark)
   A. cant
   B. cann't
   C. can't
   D. ca'nt

26. Which part of a narrative tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The beginning
   C. The middle
   D. The end

27. What did Baraka do that showed he was a good friend? (1 mark)
   A. He laughed at Omondi
   B. He told the others to stay away
   C. He explained the facts and invited Omondi to play
   D. He ran away

28. Which of these is NOT an adverb? (1 mark)
   A. early
   B. nearby
   C. tidy
   D. slowly

29. Which sentence is a direct question and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. We went home
   B. I like apples
   C. Where is the school
   D. Please close the door

30. Which conjunction gives a choice? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. and
   C. yet
   D. so

31. In which tense is a description usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Future perfect
   B. Command form
   C. Past perfect
   D. Present tense

32. Which is a better describing phrase than 'nice room'? (1 mark)
   A. a room room
   B. a room
   C. the room, room
   D. a bright, tidy room

33. What is a digital text? (1 mark)
   A. A spoken poem
   B. A text read on a screen
   C. A text printed on paper only
   D. A hand-written letter

34. Which is the correct spelling of the word used to give a reason? (1 mark)
   A. becase
   B. because
   C. becuase
   D. becouse

35. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'very pretty'? (1 mark)
   A. beutiful
   B. butiful
   C. beatiful
   D. beautiful

36. What does it mean to speak with expression? (1 mark)
   A. To speak in a whisper only
   B. To use the voice to show meaning and feeling
   C. To speak without pausing
   D. To speak very fast

37. What does 'Many hands make light work' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A job is easier when many people help
   B. Work must be light
   C. Big hands are strong
   D. Hands are heavy

38. What must a diary entry begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A title in capitals
   B. A question
   C. A friend's name
   D. The day and date

39. How is a diary different from a letter? (1 mark)
   A. A diary is always sent by post
   B. A diary always has an address
   C. A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   D. A diary has no date

40. Which word means 'jumping on one leg'? (1 mark)
   A. hopping
   B. hopped
   C. hoping
   D. hopeing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe three things you do before, while and after reading a story. (3 marks)

42. Write a short speech of four sentences about protecting a river. (4 marks)

43. Describe the steps to interpret a picture. (3 marks)

44. Explain how to use the five-finger test. (3 marks)

45. List three things a child must never give to a stranger online. (3 marks)

46. Write about 60 words about these pictures: (1) A boy plants a seed. (2) He waters it every day. (3) A tall plant grows. (5 marks)

47. Name three polite words or phrases and say when each is used. (3 marks)

48. Rewrite in the past tense: 'I watch a video and I learn a new word.' (2 marks)

49. Create a short puzzle with four clues whose answers are irregular plurals. (4 marks)

50. Describe how to find facts about a lion in a junior encyclopaedia. (4 marks)

51. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion, with an example of each. (3 marks)

52. Write two reasons why people keep diaries. (2 marks)

53. Write a title and an opening sentence for a story about a girl who finds a lost phone. (2 marks)

54. Name the three parts of a narrative and say what goes in each. (3 marks)

55. Rewrite using the past perfect: 'The bus left. Then I arrived.' (2 marks)

56. Correct the sentences: (a) 'Him is a driver.' (b) 'Give the pen to she.' (c) 'The bag is mine bag.' (3 marks)

57. Write a short talk of four sentences on how to care for a sick friend. (4 marks)

58. Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy. (4 marks)

59. Explain why 'She asked where the clinic was?' is wrong and correct it. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — /v/
   Leave ends with the voiced sound /v/.

2. D — twenty
   Twenty starts with t and w together.

3. A — a vowel sound
   We say thee egg and thuh boy.

4. C — ribbon
   Ribbon starts with /r/.

5. B — load
   Road and load both end with /əʊd/.

6. C — what happens
   The middle tells the events, including any problem.

7. A — verb
   To is followed by a verb such as sit or eat.

8. A — to make
   Use to + verb.

9. A — t
   We say lisn, so the t is silent.

10. A — the first help given to a person who is hurt or ill
   First aid is given before a doctor takes over.

11. D — The house is ours.
   Possessive pronouns are written without an apostrophe.

12. B — someone you know well
   A friendly letter is personal.

13. D — Dear
   Friendly letters begin with Dear and the name.

14. D — remember what you have read
   It records titles, dates and what you liked.

15. C — Listen politely and take turns
   Politeness keeps everyone included.

16. D — This is more beautiful than that.
   Long adjectives use more.

17. C — Beginning, middle, end
   Stories move from beginning to end.

18. D — computer
   Computer has /uː/ in its second syllable.

19. B — a colon
   For example: Baraka: I miss Grandmother.

20. C — A capital letter
   Capital letters start sentences.

21. C — Baraka clicked Send.
   Clicked is the past form.

22. C — I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   'Always' and the simple present 'ask' show a habit.

23. D — am
   'I' takes 'am' in the present progressive.

24. A — I was walking to school when it started to rain.
   Past progressive was + verb-ing, with the simple past for the shorter action.

25. C — can't
   'Cannot' becomes 'can't'.

26. B — The beginning
   The beginning introduces characters, setting and time.

27. C — He explained the facts and invited Omondi to play
   Baraka used facts to help.

28. C — tidy
   'Tidy' is an adjective.

29. C — Where is the school
   It is a direct question.

30. A — or
   'Or' offers choices.

31. D — Present tense
   Descriptions often say what something is like now.

32. D — a bright, tidy room
   Exact adjectives give a clearer picture.

33. B — A text read on a screen
   Digital texts are read on phones, tablets and computers.

34. B — because
   Because is spelt b-e-c-a-u-s-e.

35. D — beautiful
   Beautiful is spelt b-e-a-u-t-i-f-u-l.

36. B — To use the voice to show meaning and feeling
   Expression means changing loudness, stress and pitch to show feeling.

37. A — A job is easier when many people help
   Sharing work makes it easier.

38. D — The day and date
   Every entry is dated.

39. C — A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   A letter is sent to another person.

40. A — hopping
   Hopping has a double p; hoping means wishing.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before: read the title and predict. While: read slowly and find meanings of new words. After: answer questions and retell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two points such as not throwing rubbish in the river and planting trees on its bank, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each element.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, read the caption, notice details and expressions, think what is happening and what will happen next.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, home address, school name, password.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: One morning, Musa planted a seed in the garden. Every day he watered it. After some weeks, a small green shoot appeared. At last, a tall plant grew and Musa was proud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, order, linking words, past tense, punctuation and length.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Please: when asking. Thank you: when someone helps. Sorry: when we make a mistake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each phrase with its use.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: I watched a video and I learned (learnt) a new word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for watched, 1 mark for learned/learnt.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have two of these and I walk on them: feet. You chew with these: teeth. Small animals that squeak: mice. Grown-up females: women.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clue with a correct answer.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the topic Lion, find the L volume or type it in the search box, use guide words or the index to find the page, read the text, pictures and captions and write short notes in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, such as 'The club meets on Fridays.' An opinion is what someone thinks, such as 'Saving is a good idea.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remember events; to practise writing; to record feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title: An Honest Girl. One morning, Achieng found a phone near the school gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events and problem. End: how it is solved and how people felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bus had left before I arrived. (Or: When I arrived, the bus had left.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'had left' and 1 for the linking word.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) He is a driver. (b) Give the pen to her. (c) The bag is mine. / It is my bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two caring actions such as visiting and listening, and a closing thank-you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the four parts.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reports a question, so it is a statement and needs a full stop. Correct: She asked where the clinic was.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reason, 1 for correction, 1 for full stop.
